title: I spent 4 years building my dream pirate MMO, then put it on hold to raise my kids. AI helped me bring it back.
author: igotlagg
selftext:
Seven years ago, I started working on my dream game: a multiplayer pirate world where players could sail, explore, fight, and build their own adventures.

About two years ago, I had to put the project aside. Life got busy, we had kids, and between work and family, there simply weren't enough hours in the day.

Honestly, I thought I'd never find the time to work on it again, but recently, AI development has made a huge difference. It's helping me tackle things that previously would have taken weeks, and suddenly I'm making real progress again.

There's still a long way to go, but seeing my little pirate world come back to life after all this time feels incredible.

Here's some actual gameplay from the current build. I'd love to hear what you think!

replies.author: igotlagg
replies.body:
Yea, i will. To be honest, my friends and me typed out 70 ish real quests with dialogues in xml format. (Dont judge past me for choosing xml in simpler times).

We had nights where de gathered, drank rum, tried to speak in some lines, boy, it was horrible. But we had so much fun.

Now I just slapped some med text to speech model on it. It works. Its far from perfect, and I will use a better one when development is done, but man, is it already miles ahead of our real voice overs lol

comments.author: WhatchuMean69
comments.body: Looks very nice! How does your workflow look like? How much you spend, if you don't mind me asking?

replies.author: igotlagg
replies.body:
well for startes, I had an entire code base to look into (Software architect/engineer by day, game dev by night). I started by migrating it to threejs from Unity, and fixed bugs or incompleteness along the way.

From then on Claude had a feeling about my preferences, and just went along with my infrastructure as I asked it to add stuff in human like language. It's far from perfect so I iterate a lot. I start a session, write everything that bugs me or is wrong down, feed it into seperate Claude sessions and they all start spinning up their own server to work their issue on.

When I have 8 prallel chats, my PC gets roasted (I have 100GB RAM, i9 intel CPU workstation, but only GT1080 GPU). but it does it job, and all I have to do is playtest for an hour, gather info, feed AI.. repeat.

It's been a week. As said before, it's based on an existing code base, but I still review every code change, and without my software engineer background, this wasn't possible to develop as robust and quickly as now.

replies.author: WhatchuMean69
replies.body: Thank you for the detailed answer. Good luck on your game and everything else!

replies.author: igotlagg
replies.body: OH! What I spent? I have a $200 Claude subscription and it barely used a weekly limit (I use it for my job too so I cannot use it all on Plunder). So, $30 worth of subscription value?
